title: A 320×256 6.9mW 2.2mK-NETD 120.4dB-DR LW-IRFPA with Pixel-Paralleled Light-Driven 20b Current-to-Phase ADC
problem: Long-wavelength cryogenic infrared focal plane arrays (LW-IRFPA) require high dynamic range readout circuits (ROIC) to improve signal-to-noise ratio, but conventional current-voltage or current-frequency modulation rely on power-hungry analog circuits susceptible to interference and crosstalk from long data buses. Prior ROICs consume significant power in analog circuits and data transfer.
motivation: Cryogenic infrared imaging demands sensitive, low-noise readout with high well capacity; prior analog-intensive designs waste power and introduce crosstalk, limiting SNR and sensitivity performance required for scientific/military thermal imaging.
method: Pixel-paralleled light-driven current-to-phase ADC (IP-ADC) architecture with four key components: (1) light-current-controlled oscillator (LCO) modulator powered only by photocurrent without extra supply, (2) phase-reconstruction circuit with sub-phase extraction to enhance low-light performance and reduce quantization noise, (3) pixel-level 20-bit asynchronous gray-code counter for high equivalent full-well capacity, and (4) low-swing bus data transfer circuit to reduce transmission power and crosstalk. Fabricated in 0.18μm CMOS for a 320×256 array with 30μm pixel pitch and QWIP detectors.
key_novelty: Light-current-driven (photocurrent-powered) modulator for current-to-phase conversion eliminating need for external power supply and enabling pixel-parallel ADC with no global analog circuits.
contributions: Pixel-paralleled IP-ADC architecture powered by photocurrent alone, eliminating power-hungry global analog circuits and interference
Light-current-controlled oscillator (LCO) modulator as core power-free analog front-end
Phase-reconstruction with sub-phase extraction improving low-light performance and reducing quantization noise
Low-swing bus architecture reducing data transmission power and crosstalk
Ultra-low power ROIC: 6.9mW for full 320×256 array with 120.4dB dynamic range and 2.2mK NETD
limitations: Not discussed—frame rate, integration time, quantum efficiency, and readout noise specifications not stated in abstract.
primary_theme: Power-efficient photocurrent-driven ADC for infrared focal plane arrays
